Coffee With Kyria Spiridoula

Kyria Spiridoula shamelessly shows various jellyfish stings — in her armpit, on her breast, on her stomach. She gestures a lot when she talks. They have finally put up nets against the jellyfish. But there are still jellyfish inside, and Kyria Spiridoula certainly isn’t going to swim where everyone is swimming now and a hundred people are pissing in the sea. As a child, she spent her summers near Patras. There were wonderful beaches there! Lonely, secret beaches. You could lie around naked there all day.

It is a Sunday morning in July. I don’t know Kyria Spiridoula; by chance, a friend called me over to the table. Kyria Spiridoula is drinking Greek coffee. We are having orange juice and Freddo espresso.

*All in this Together*, was inspired by the tough times that we go through in our lives, not just as individuals but together as a community. Last year, my home province of Nova Scotia suffered through a terrible drought, and with it horrific wildfires. But we as people stand strong and tall through it all, just like our beautiful buildings, which can be seen in this piece.

*Planet curious*, Acrylic on canvas, 60 × 80cm, 2025

Curiosity positioned as a cosmology. An endless appetite for experience as the artist's defining condition. Part of the series Can I Be a Rainbow?, *Planet Curious* xplores that same restless wondering, the refusal to arrive anywhere fully. Scan it with Artivive-APP and the painting wakes up, its hidden layers shifting into motion.

*Sonoma* is a digital drawing of the Sonoma Valley, based on the default desktop background on my Mac. Following what seems to be a painterly instinct when faced with the beauty of a landscape, I tried to capture the rolling wine hills of Sonoma by drawing with my mouse and using the pipette tool to pick colours directly from my screen.

119 Cheung Sha Wan Road 長沙灣道119號

This was the first apartment I shared with my friend Ria after our graduation. I’ve lived in several different places and recently I decided to move out of my current apartment without knowing my next long-term residence. It feels a bit weird to be “homeless” in your 30s. And the hardest part would be categorizing your belongings you have hoarded in the past 10 years and decided which are of less important while others are to be kept.

My roommate told me that she is yearning for a home and she has to leave Hong Kong so that Hong Kong can be that “home” she is yearning for. I agree with her.

*Glacier 3000*, Tsanfleuron Glacier, Switzerland · 2026

Between ice and stone, the landscape records its own disappearance. Human intervention appears only as a small trace within a process unfolding over centuries. Scale becomes uncertain, and elsewhere begins where certainty ends.

This image was created to occupy a place temporarily. The circle represented no object, the country was assigned without intention, and the number belonged to an entry that had not yet arrived.

It was expected to disappear. Instead, during the construction of the archive, the placeholder was invited to remain. What had been made to represent absence became an entry of its own. I chose not to correct the image or its assigned country: both are traces of the conditions under which the archive came into being.

Not everything elsewhere needs to be found.
